title: Facebook Ads for Local Businesses: The 2026 Playbook

facts.fact: The article was published on April 13, 2026.
The article's campaign blueprint diagram lists four main Facebook ad campaign objectives: Awareness, Traffic, Leads, and Sales/Conversions.
facts.quote: A strategic blueprint diagram detailing the four main Facebook ad campaign objectives: Awareness, Traffic, Leads, and Sales/Conversions.

facts.fact: The article says Leads is the best-fit objective when a service business sells through calls or forms, because it removes friction and captures intent directly inside Meta.
facts.quote: Service business that sells through calls or forms | **Leads** | Removes friction and captures intent directly inside Meta

facts.fact: The article recommends the Awareness objective for a new location or new market presence where people do not yet know the business exists.
facts.quote: New location, low awareness in a tight area | **Awareness** | Puts the brand in front of nearby residents before asking for action

facts.fact: According to Neil Patel's small business Facebook ads guide, local businesses can waste up to 62% of ad spend on poor targeting.
facts.quote: Local businesses can waste up to 62% of ad spend on poor targeting

facts.fact: According to Neil Patel's small business Facebook ads guide, hyper-specific behavioral and interest layering can yield 2.5x higher conversion rates compared to broad demographics alone.
facts.quote: hyper-specific behavioral and interest layering can yield 2.5x higher conversion rates compared to broad demographics alone

facts.fact: The author's example budget preference for many local accounts is $40 a day behind one serious offer rather than $10 a day spread across four ad sets.
facts.quote: For many local accounts, I would rather see $40 a day behind one serious offer than $10 a day spread across four ad sets that never exit the learning phase.
